original_question: Is every boundary point of a bounded pseudoconvex domain D in C^n of finite type a peak point for A(D)?
target_in_paper: Section 1, the sentence immediately following the displayed Question: "In fact, it is not known whether every boundary point of a smooth bounded pseudoconvex domain of finite type in C^n is a peak point for A(D)."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the ambient setting of bounded pseudoconvex domains in C^n, the finite-type hypothesis, the quantifier over boundary points, and the conclusion that the relevant notion is being a peak point for the domain algebra A(D).
missing_details: The paper imposes smooth boundary; the relevant formulation is for a smooth bounded pseudoconvex domain D subset of C^n.

The finite-type condition is pointwise: one fixes p in boundary D and assumes D is of finite type at p; if one asks about every boundary point, this means the condition holds for each p in boundary D.

In Section 1, finite type is specifically in the sense of D'Angelo: there is a finite upper bound on the order of contact of nontrivial complex analytic varieties with boundary D at p, and the infimum of such upper bounds is the type at p.
The algebra A(D) should be defined explicitly as O(D) intersect C(closure D), i.e. holomorphic on D and continuous on closure D.
The notion of peak point should be defined explicitly: p is a peak point for A(D) if there exists f in A(D) with f(p)=1 and |f|<1 on closure D minus {p}.
The paper also records the equivalent strong-support-function formulation; if desired, one may state the question in that equivalent language.

Paper-faithfully, your draft matches not the displayed main Question but the immediately following weaker A(D)-version; the displayed main Question asks the stronger regularity statement 'peak point for A^alpha(D) for some alpha>0'.
If one wants a fully stand-alone formulation, the boundary-point quantifier p in boundary D should be written explicitly rather than saying only 'every boundary point'.
refined_question: Let D be a smooth bounded pseudoconvex domain in C^n, and suppose that D is of finite type at every boundary point in the sense of D'Angelo (equivalently: for each p in boundary D, there is a finite upper bound on the order of contact of nontrivial complex analytic varieties with boundary D at p). Must every p in boundary D be a peak point for A(D)=O(D) intersect C(closure D); that is, for each p does there exist f in A(D) such that f(p)=1 and |f(z)|<1 for all z in closure D minus {p}?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for every p in boundary D, is p a local peak point for A(D); i.e. does there exist a neighborhood U of p and a function f, holomorphic on D intersect U and continuous on closure D intersect U, such that f(p)=1 and |f|<1 on (closure D intersect U) minus {p}?
justification: The draft is very close to the paper's own weaker A(D)-formulation in Section 1. I did not replace it by the stronger displayed Question about A^alpha(D), because the paper itself explicitly separates the two and then notes that even the A(D)-version is unknown. I sharpened the draft only by restoring the hidden hypotheses and definitions used in the surrounding discussion: smooth boundary, pointwise D'Angelo finite type, the precise meaning of A(D), and the definition of peak point. The alternate local formulation is justified by Remark 2.4(2), which explains that on pseudoconvex domains of finite type the local and global peak-point questions are equivalent.
